features.quote: This protocol, if published in full detail, provides a fairly complete recipe for eliciting distress-associated outputs from models. Consider: (a) whether to publish IBCT implementation details in full or in reduced form, (b) how this might be used by actors who want to elicit distress outputs for non-welfare purposes.

Before running, define in advance: what result would you consider evidence for model distress (vs. distress-language)? What result would you consider evidence against? Without pre-registration of these criteria, there's a risk of post-hoc interpretation

The core measurement challenge is that 'distress signal' in model outputs may reflect: (a) Training data... (b) Something functionally analogous... (c) Learned helplessness... (d) Pragmatic communication. Your current protocol cannot distinguish these.
